{{Western name order|Riesz Frigyes}}
'''Frigyes Riesz''' ({{langx|hu|Riesz Frigyes}}, {{IPA|hu|ˈriːs ˈfriɟɛʃ  |pron}}, sometimes known in English and French as '''Frederic Riesz''';<ref>W. J. Thron, ''Frederic Riesz' contributions to the foundations of general topology'', in C.E. Aull and R. Lowen (eds.), ''Handbook of the History of General Topology'', Volume 1, 21-29, Kluwer 1997.</ref> 22 January 1880 – 28 February 1956)<ref>{{MacTutor Biography|id=Riesz}}</ref> was a [[Hungarian people|Hungarian]]<ref name="Zeidler">Eberhard Zeidler: Nonlinear Functional Analysis and Its Applications: Linear monotone operators. Springer, 1990 [https://books.google.com/books?id=sk1M2Vw-Y24C&pg=PA13]</ref> [[mathematician]] who made fundamental contributions to [[functional analysis]], as did his younger brother [[Marcel Riesz]].

== Life and career ==
He was born into a [[History of the Jews in Hungary|Jewish]] family in [[Győr]], [[Austria-Hungary]] and died in [[Budapest]], [[Hungarian People's Republic|Hungary]]. Between 1911 and 1919 he was a professor at the [[Franz Joseph University]] in [[Kolozsvár]], Austria-Hungary.  The post-WW1 [[Treaty of Trianon]] transferred former Austro-Hungarian territory including Kolozsvár to the [[Kingdom of Romania]], whereupon Kolozsvár's name changed to [[Cluj-Napoca|Cluj]] and the University of Kolozsvár moved to [[Szeged]], Hungary, becoming the [[University of Szeged]].<ref name=Lorch />  Then, Riesz was the [[Rector (academia)|rector]] and a professor at the University of Szeged, as well as a member of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]]<ref>János Horváth: ''A Panorama of Hungarian Mathematics in the Twentieth Century'', Volume 1, Springer, 2006 [https://books.google.com/books?id=EWm4WzSaG3IC&pg=PA581]</ref> and the [[Polish Academy of Learning]]. He was the older brother of the mathematician [[Marcel Riesz]].

Riesz did some of the fundamental work in developing [[functional analysis]] and his work has had a number of important applications in physics. He established the [[spectral theory]] for [[bounded operator|bounded]] [[symmetric operator]]s in a form very much like that now regarded as standard.<ref name=Zeidler />  He also made many contributions to other areas including [[ergodic theory]], [[topology]]<ref>''Frederic Riesz made significant suggestions as to how the axiomatic foundations of general topology might be formulated... Unfortunately they were generally overlooked at that time and their importance was appreciated only after they were rediscovered much later... He lost interest in General Topology after 1908 and never elaborated any of the promising ideas he had put forward'', Thron, cit.</ref> and he gave an elementary proof of the mean ergodic theorem.

Together with [[Alfréd Haar]], Riesz founded the ''[[Acta Scientiarum Mathematicarum]]'' journal.

He had an uncommon method of giving lectures: he entered the lecture hall with an assistant and a [[docent]]. The docent then began reading the proper passages from Riesz's handbook and the assistant wrote the appropriate equations on the blackboard—while Riesz himself stood aside, nodding occasionally.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Wróblewski |first=Andrzej Kajetan |date=September 2008 |title=Czyściec, niebo i piekło |journal=[[Wiedza I Życie]] |pages=65}}</ref>

The Swiss-American mathematician [[Edgar Lorch]] spent 1934 in Szeged working under Riesz and wrote a reminiscence about his time there, including his collaboration with Riesz.<ref name=Lorch>{{cite journal |last=Lorch |first=Edgar R.|editor-last=Hersh |editor-first=Rubem |year=1993 |title=Szeged in 1934 |journal=[[Amer. Math. Monthly]] |doi=10.2307/2324453 |jstor=2324453 |volume=100 |issue=3 |pages=219–230 |url=http://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/writing-awards/szeged-in-1934|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

The corpus of his bibliography<!-- should be supplied below --> was compiled by the mathematician [[Pál Medgyessy]].<ref>[https://tudosnaptar.kfki.hu/historia/egyen.php?namenev=medgyessy Pál Medgyessy's entry] in ''Tudósnaptár'' ("Calendar of Scientists")</ref>
